top_temples.name: Thakurbari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Gangtok Bazaar; built in 1935 on land donated by the Chogyal (Namgyal dynasty ruler); one of the oldest Hindu temples in Sikkim, confirmed on the official state list of Hindu mandirs.

top_temples.name: Ganesh Tok
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop shrine at about 6,500 ft on the Gangtok ridge, known for panoramic views.

top_temples.name: Hanuman Tok
top_temples.deity: Hanuman (with a Durga shrine on the premises)
top_temples.location_note: About 5 km from White Hall on the Gangtok-Nathula highway, at roughly 7,200 ft; built with Indian Army involvement.

top_temples.name: Durga Mandir, Gangtok
top_temples.location_note: Established in 1986; active mainly around festival days per local reporting.

top_temples.name: Shri Siddheshwar Shiv Mandir (Pani House)
top_temples.location_note: Pani House area of Gangtok; centered on a natural stone Shivlingam said to have been worshipped there for a long time. Corresponds to the 'Pani House Nag Devi Mandir, Gangtok' entry on the official state list of Hindu mandirs.

top_temples.name: Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: At Legshep near Geyzing/Gyalshing, on the banks of the River Rangeet; one of Sikkim's oldest temples, tied to a Mahabharata-era legend of Shiva appearing as a hunter (Kirat). Listed officially as 'Legshep Kirateswar Maha Dev Mandir' under Gyalshing sub-division.

top_temples.name: Gyalshing Singha Devi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Located in Gyalshing (Geyzing) town itself, per the official state list of Hindu mandirs.

top_temples.name: Mangan Pashupatinath Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Mangan Bazaar; confirmed on the official state list of Hindu mandirs for the Mangan sub-division.

top_temples.name: Shiv Mandir, B-II
top_temples.location_note: B-II locality, Mangan sub-division; confirmed on the official state list of Hindu mandirs.

top_temples.name: Siddhesvara Dham (Char Dham Temple)
top_temples.deity: Shiva, with a full Char Dham replica complex (Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri, Rameswaram) and a Sai Baba mandir
top_temples.location_note: On Solophok Hill, about 5 km from Namchi; inaugurated 2011; features a 108 ft Shiva statue with the 12 jyotirlingas. Officially listed as 'Siddhesvara Char Dhaam, Solophok, Namchi.'

top_temples.name: Namchi Pashupatinath Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Namchi town itself, per the official state list of Hindu mandirs.

top_temples.name: Pemayangtse Monastery
top_temples.deity: Nyingma order of Tibetan Buddhism (Guru Rinpoche lineage)
top_temples.location_note: Founded 1647 by Lama Lhatsun Chempo near Pelling; one of Sikkim's oldest and most important monasteries, historically head of the Nyingma order's monasteries in Sikkim.

top_temples.name: Sangachoeling Monastery
top_temples.location_note: On a ridge above Pelling, close to Pemayangtse; regarded as the second-oldest monastery in Sikkim.

top_temples.name: Rumtek Monastery (Dharma Chakra Centre)
top_temples.deity: Karma Kagyu order of Tibetan Buddhism
top_temples.location_note: Originally founded 1734 by the 9th Karmapa; rebuilt 1966 by the 16th Karmapa as the Dharma Chakra Centre; the seat-in-exile of the Karmapa and the largest monastery in Sikkim.

top_temples.name: Old Rumtek Monastery
top_temples.deity: Karma Kagyu order of Tibetan Buddhism
top_temples.location_note: The original, smaller 18th-century structure near the present-day Rumtek Monastery, predating the 1960s rebuild.

top_temples.name: Soreng Thakurbari
top_temples.location_note: Located in Soreng town itself, per the official state list of Hindu mandirs.

top_temples.name: Narsing Kali Devi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Located in Soreng town itself, per the official state list of Hindu mandirs.

top_temples.name: Tadong Durga Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Tadong, Gangtok; confirmed on the official state list of Hindu mandirs.

top_temples.name: Tadong Jaganath Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Tadong, Gangtok; confirmed on the official state list of Hindu mandirs.
